sections.title: EPRA Performance & Capital Structure
sections.subtitle: EPRA earnings/EPS strip out the IFRS revaluation line that dominates reported net income for a REIT; LTV and interest cover are the leverage metrics management targets against its own guiderails.

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Hammerson plc: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Hammerson plc: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Hammerson plc: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Hammerson plc: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Hammerson plc: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

epraEarnings.title: EPRA earnings vs net income
epraEarnings.content:
EPRA earnings is the industry-standard REIT profit measure: recurring rental profit after interest and tax, excluding fair-value revaluations, disposal gains/losses and other one-offs. IFRS net income includes all of that, so for a property company it swings on the valuer's opinion of the portfolio as much as on trading.

For Hammerson: FY2023-24 net income was deeply negative on portfolio write-downs even as the flagship destinations kept trading; FY2025 EPRA earnings of £104.3m rose only modestly while IFRS net income swung to +£232.1m mostly on reversing write-downs. Management guides FY2026 EPRA earnings growth of c.27% to c.£132m -- that is the number to track, not the IFRS line.

What to watch:

  • EPRA earnings growth versus the guided c.27% for FY2026
  • How much of any IFRS net income swing is a revaluation, not trading

epraEps.title: EPRA EPS vs reported EPS
epraEps.content:
EPRA EPS is EPRA earnings per share -- the basis for Hammerson's dividend and its new medium-term growth target. Reported EPS includes the same revaluation and one-off noise as IFRS net income.

For Hammerson: new CEO guidance (July 2026) targets 6-8% EPRA EPS CAGR and 6-8% DPS CAGR off the FY2025 base, with the dividend paid at 80-85% of full-year EPRA earnings -- so EPRA EPS, not reported EPS, is what funds the distribution.

What to watch:

  • EPRA EPS growth against the 6-8% CAGR target
  • Dividend per share tracking EPRA EPS rather than outrunning it

leverage.title: LTV and interest cover
leverage.content:
LTV (loan-to-value) is net debt divided by portfolio value; interest cover is EPRA earnings before interest divided by net finance costs. Both are the leverage/solvency pair that REIT lenders and rating agencies watch.

For Hammerson: management's own through-the-cycle guiderails are c.35% LTV and 6-8x net debt:EBITDA; LTV was 39% and net debt:EBITDA 8.1x (annualised) at H1 2026 -- above guiderail, which management attributes to the Arndale acquisition and expects to unwind as disposals and annualisation complete (pro forma net debt:EBITDA already back to c.7x). The FY2025 viability stress test showed interest-cover covenant headroom to a 75% fall in net rental income.

What to watch:

  • LTV and net debt:EBITDA converging back toward the 35% / 6-8x guiderails
  • Interest cover trend as the c.£60m FY2026 net finance cost guide plays out

nri.title: Net rental income
nri.content:
Net rental income (NRI) is rent and related income from the properties less direct property costs -- the core operating line before overheads, interest and revaluations.

For Hammerson: H1 2026 group NRI was £112m, +40% YoY, driven by buying out joint-venture partners (full consolidation of destinations previously held 50/50) plus the Manchester Arndale acquisition and c.5% like-for-like growth from leasing and occupancy. Guidance is for c.28% total NRI growth and c.4-5% like-for-like growth in FY2026.

What to watch:

  • Like-for-like NRI growth (the organic number) versus total NRI growth (includes acquisitions/JV buyouts)
  • Occupancy and leasing spreads feeding through to NRI with a lag

nta.title: NTA per share
nta.content:
NTA per share is net tangible assets divided by shares -- the book value of the portfolio.

For Hammerson plc: the share price relative to NTA is the market's view of the portfolio's valuation and management.

What to watch:

  • Discount or premium to NTA
  • NTA growth from revaluations versus retained cash

occupancy.title: Occupancy
occupancy.content:
The share of lettable space (or units) that is leased.

For Hammerson plc: occupancy below the sector norm is the first sign of rental pressure.

What to watch:

  • Occupancy trend
  • Lease expiries in the next two years

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Hammerson plc: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Hammerson plc: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Hammerson plc: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Hammerson plc: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
